young.html: On a magical island live a magician named Prospero, his daughter Miranda, an airy spirit called Ariel, and a creature named Caliban. Twelve years ago, Prospero's brother stole his dukedom in Italy and set him and baby Miranda adrift in a boat. They washed up here.

Now a ship carrying Prospero's old enemies sails near. Prospero raises a great storm, a tempest, and the ship is wrecked, but Ariel makes sure no one is hurt. On the island, the king's son meets Miranda and they fall in love. Prospero could take his revenge. Instead, he chooses to forgive.

young.text:
O, wonder!
How many goodly creatures are there here!
How beauteous mankind is! O brave new world
That has such people in 't!
young.author: William Shakespeare
young.ed: First printed in the First Folio

full.html: Late in his career, around 1608–1611, Shakespeare wrote four plays now often called romances: Pericles, Cymbeline, The Winter's Tale and The Tempest. They share sea voyages, lost children found again, long years of separation, wonders, and forgiveness. The Tempest, probably the last play he wrote alone, was printed first in the First Folio.

full.html: Prospero controls everything on the island through his magic and Ariel's help. He brings his enemies to the edge of despair, and then, at the turn of Act V, he chooses mercy.

full.text:
Yet with my nobler reason 'gainst my fury
Do I take part: the rarer action is
In virtue than in vengeance: they being penitent,
full.author: William Shakespeare
full.ed: First printed in the First Folio
full.note: The sentence goes on: since they repent, he will go no further. Spelling and punctuation as in the Project Gutenberg text, which modernizes the early printings.

full.html: He forgives his brother Antonio, the King of Naples and the others, frees Ariel, and says he will break his staff and drown his book of magic. In the epilogue he steps forward and asks the audience to set him free with their applause.

full.text:
Our revels now are ended. These our actors,
As I foretold you, were all spirits and
Are melted into air, into thin air: ...
We are such stuff
As dreams are made on, and our little life
Is rounded with a sleep.
full.author: William Shakespeare
full.ed: First printed in the First Folio
full.note: Shortened: lines are left out after "thin air." Spelling and punctuation as in the Project Gutenberg text, which modernizes the early printings.

full.html: Prospero speaks after ending a magical show for the young couple. The whole world, he says, will one day fade like a play. Many readers have heard in it Shakespeare's own farewell to the theater, though no one can prove that.

Caliban says the island was his until Prospero came and made him a servant. Prospero says he taught Caliban and was repaid with betrayal. Since the 1800s and especially in the last century, readers and directors have discussed the play in light of European voyages and colonies, while others read Caliban mainly as a figure of untaught nature. The play gives Caliban some of its most beautiful lines about the island's music.
Thinking Prospero is simply good. He is also harsh and controlling, and the play lets us see it. His choice to forgive matters because he could do otherwise.

deep.html: Shakespeare seems to have read accounts of a 1609 shipwreck in Bermuda, and he borrowed from Montaigne's "Of Cannibals" (in Florio's 1603 translation) for Gonzalo's dream of an ideal commonwealth. Earlier on this ladder, Virgil's Aeneid begins with a storm and a shipwreck too.

items: Is forgiveness "rarer" and nobler than revenge? Is it always right to forgive?
What does Prospero owe Ariel and Caliban? Who has the right to rule the island?
Why does Prospero give up his magic? What would you give up, and why?

questions: Prospero could have taken revenge but chose to forgive. Why is forgiving sometimes harder than getting even?
Miranda calls the world "brave" and "new." What would you think if you saw the world for the first time?
Ariel wants to be free. Caliban wants his island back. Do they both have a fair claim?
Prospero says life is like a dream. What do you think he means?
